Subject: Post-call: FinWave model-fit & quantization tradeoffs / next steps

Hi Alice & Samir,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and recommended next steps from my side:

Recap
- Goal: 1) Replace FinWave's on-prem QA assistant with a hosted/dedicated Redwood endpoint that meets 200ms median latency and <2% quality regression on your internal evaluation set.
- Workload: mix of short prompts (~30-150 tokens) with some long-context retrieval chains (~2k tokens).
- Constraints: SOC2 + data residency, procurement timeline ~Q3.

Model / eval recommendations
- Baseline models to try (we recommend running evals on all three):
  1) Mistral-7B-Instruct (FP16 baseline) — good raw quality / cheap ops.
  2) Llama-3-13B-Chat (FP16 baseline) — stronger long-form/context handling, higher cost.
  3) Falcon-40B (for high-fidelity benchmarks if you want to push quality ceilings)

Quantization & throughput options (summary)
- AWQ (4-bit asymmetric): highest throughput gains with minimal loss on many instruct tasks; recommended first-pass on Mistral-7B.
- GPTQ (4-bit): sometimes yields larger quality variance across prompts; more engineering to stabilize on some architectures.
- FP8 (hardware FP8, A100/H100 optimized): excellent throughput but requires HW-specific kernels and careful calibration; best for Dedicated/AWS clusters.

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a starter prompt set (finwave_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) — please confirm it's representative.
2) We'll run a 48-hour bench on your representative corpus (compare FP16 baseline vs AWQ-4 vs GPTQ-4 for Mistral-7B; include Llama-3-13B FP16 as a reference).
3) Schedule a SRE/NetOps quick call to confirm egress/residency for Private deployment (if needed).

Proposed timeline
- Confirm prompt set & sample data: 2 business days
- Bench run: 2 business days
- Review & recommendation: 1 business day

I've looped Rishi (AE) for procurement and Vivek (SRE/bench) for the eval. Evelyn from CS will own the handoff if we move to pilot.

Would you like us to start the bench on Wednesday 30th?

Thanks,
Marissa

Alice — thanks, answers inline and attached a short bench report + the prompt set we discussed. Attachments: quant-bench-report-20270630.pdf, finwave_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

Short answers
- p95 latency (single-user interactive expectations) — rough numbers from our Mistral-7B bench (T4-equivalent / single-stream):
- FP16 baseline: p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 420ms
- AWQ-4: p50 ~ 90ms, p95 ~ 220ms (observed ~2-3x throughput gain; p95 improvements driven by reduced per-token compute)
- GPTQ-4: p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 280ms (more variance across prompt types; some long-context prompts saw higher degradation)

- Quality deltas (EM-style extraction / slot fills) observed vs FP16 baseline on our internal eval subset (Mistral-7B):
- AWQ-4: average absolute EM drop ~ 1.2% (range 0.2–2.6% depending on prompt class)
- GPTQ-4: average absolute EM drop ~ 2.8% (range 0.5–6.5%)
- FP8 (hw): <1% drop on well-calibrated kernels but requires Dedicated + kernel support

Notes and recommendations
- Recommendation: Start with AWQ-4 on Mistral-7B for the pilot. It gives the best throughput/quality tradeoff and is fastest to iterate on.
- Keep Llama-3-13B FP16 as a reference for higher quality needs; if slot-fills are sensitive, test Llama-3-13B on a subset.
- If FinWave decides to commit to Dedicated (A100/H100), we can explore FP8 for additional gains (engineering cost: kernel work + calibration).

Next steps (action items)
- Vivek: start the bench Wednesday 30th against the attached prompt set; compare FP16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4 for Mistral-7B. Upload raw bench results to the Drive folder linked below.
- Rishi: I flagged procurement — can you send a ballpark 3-month pilot cost for hosted + one Dedicated instance?
- Evelyn: prepare an onboarding checklist for CS; we'll align once bench confirms model choice.

Links
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinWaveEval (bench artifacts and raw logs)
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FW-2311

Will start the bench now unless I hear otherwise.

Thanks,
Marissa
